classification.difficultyReason: Calculate a vertical climb, interpret it and compare it with the required increase in altitude.

content.prompt: An aeroplane flying at an altitude of $1500\text{ m}$ starts to climb at an angle of $15^\circ$ to the horizontal when the pilot sees a mountain peak $2120\text{ m}$ high, $2400\text{ m}$ away from him horizontally.

spec.description: Unshaded mountain and schematic aeroplane, with the aeroplane vertically above Q and mountain peak M vertically above N. Both ground points lie on one horizontal baseline.
spec.mathematics: QN is 2400 m horizontally; the aeroplane altitude is 1500 m and MN is 2120 m. The mountain summit is above the plane's initial altitude.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and point labels are visible.

spec.description: Right triangle with H/O/A labels and a lower dashed projection showing the initial altitude and horizontal distance. The left angle is 15 degrees and the opposite side is x metres.
spec.mathematics: The horizontal adjacent side is 2400 m; the opposite side is x m; the hypotenuse rises at 15 degrees. The lower baseline is 1500 m below the adjacent side.
spec.answerVisibility: The unknown x is retained; no calculated climb or clearance is shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the value of $x$ to 2 decimal places. What does this represent?

answer.short: $x\approx643.08\text{ m}$. This is the vertical climb over a horizontal distance of $2400\text{ m}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\tan15^\circ&=\frac{x}{2400}\\x&=2400\tan15^\circ\\x&\approx643.08\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
This is the increase in the aeroplane's altitude while it travels $2400\text{ m}$ horizontally.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Will the aeroplane clear the mountain?

answer.short: Yes. The required climb is $620\text{ m}$, less than $2400\tan15^\circ\text{ m}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Required climb}&=2120-1500\\&=620\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Since $2400\tan15^\circ>620$, the aeroplane will clear the mountain.
